title: Diabetic kidney disease

steps.tx: Early diabetic nephropathy begins with glomerular **hyperfiltration** driven by enhanced proximal sodium-glucose cotransport via **SGLT2**, which diminishes distal sodium chloride delivery to the macula densa. This blunts tubuloglomerular feedback, triggering **afferent arteriolar** vasodilation and angiotensin II-mediated efferent arteriolar vasoconstriction that elevates intraglomerular capillary pressure.

steps.tx: Pathognomonic histological features of advanced diabetic glomerulosclerosis comprise diffuse mesangial matrix expansion and nodular intercapillary glomerulosclerosis, termed **Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules**. These rounded, acellular, PAS-positive, and silver-positive nodules arise from capillary microaneurysm organization and progressive mesangial expansion, accompanied by prominent **arteriolar hyalinosis**.

steps.tx: Annual screening for diabetic kidney disease requires measuring the spot urinary **albumin-to-creatinine ratio** (**uACR**) in an early morning specimen. Microalbuminuria (moderately increased albuminuria) is defined as **30** to **300** mg/g creatinine, whereas macroalbuminuria (severely increased albuminuria) is confirmed when uACR exceeds **300** mg/g in two of three samples.

rows: Early microvascular disease, high CV risk

steps.tx: Landmark clinical trials including CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, and EMPA-KIDNEY establish that **SGLT2 inhibitors** (**dapagliflozin**, empagliflozin, canagliflozin) significantly slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular death in diabetic kidney disease. By restoring macula densa sodium delivery, they reactivate **tubuloglomerular feedback**, promoting afferent vasoconstriction that normalizes intraglomerular pressure. Kidney failure falls by **30%** to **40%**.

right.title: ACE Inhibitor Actions
points: Reduces systemic blood pressure and proteinuria

steps.tx: The non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist **Finerenone** demonstrated significant kidney and cardiovascular protective efficacy in the **FIDELIO-DKD** and FIGARO-DKD clinical trials. In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD receiving maximum tolerated RAAS inhibition, finerenone significantly reduced **albuminuria** and slowed renal disease progression by blunting aldosterone-mediated inflammation and fibrosis.

right.title: Diagnostic Features
points: GFR criteria evaluated per 1.73 m2 body surface

steps.tx: Clinical suspicion of **non-diabetic kidney disease** (**NDKD**) warrants kidney biopsy in diabetic patients presenting with atypical features. These include absence of **diabetic retinopathy** (especially in type 1 diabetes), sudden onset of nephrotic-range proteinuria, rapid unexplained GFR decline, active urinary sediment with red blood cell casts, or systemic signs of vasculitis.

left.title: Atypical Red Flags for NDKD
points: Active urinary sediment with RBC casts
Onset of nephrotic syndrome < 5 years in T1D

right.title: Typical DKD Course
points: Slow, progressive GFR decline over years
Bland sediment with broad granular casts

steps.tx: First-line pharmacotherapy for hypertension and albuminuria in diabetic kidney disease utilizes **ACE inhibitors** or **ARBs**, titrated to the maximum tolerated dose. Dual combination therapy using an ACE inhibitor together with an ARB is strictly contraindicated because the **VA NEPHRON-D** and ONTARGET trials demonstrated heightened risks of hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury without benefit.

left.title: Recommended Monotherapy
points: Single ACE inhibitor or ARB agent

right.title: Contraindicated Dual Blockade
points: Higher incidence of acute renal failure

steps.tx: Diabetic kidney disease is the most common cause of **Type 4 renal tubular acidosis**, characterized by hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism presenting with **hyperkalemic normal anion gap** metabolic acidosis. Impaired renin release from hyalinized juxtaglomerular apparatuses leads to deficient aldosterone production, exacerbating hyperkalemia even at modest degrees of renal insufficiency.
